Different robust combination from trimmed_mean: median picks the single central forecast per horizon, testing whether more aggressive center-selection helps given the wide error spread (20x) and moderate ranking stability (tau=0.47).
Top-5 SMAPE pool mean: tighter pool avoids noisy tail models; diverse clusters (rf, DWT_catboost, DWT_rf, ONLY_CWT_catboost, ONLY_FT_rf) complement each other
Diagnosis hints weighted; moderate ranking stability means a soft tilt within the top-5 pool should be stable and may beat equal mean.
DBA adapts per-horizon to capture the shifting best model across windows (tau=0.47); different kind from mean/weighted already tested on pool4
Per-horizon top-5 selection on the 7-model pool; tests whether horizon-adaptive weighting exploits the moderate ranking instability (tau=0.47) better than fixed softmax on the 5-model pool.
error_trend weighting on pool4: rewards models improving across windows, complementing the static softmax leader
meta_model learned weights on pool4 (series scope, smape metric) - different kind of weighting than error_trend/softmax already tested; leverages cross-series structure to allocate shares
per-horizon top-3 selection on pool4: exploits moderate ranking instability (tau=0.47) where different models excel at different horizons
Robust median on pool4 to test whether pool selection alone (without weight estimation) captures most of the benefit, given high-variance weight estimation with only 3 windows

inverse_error weighting on pool4: simplest robust scheme using aggregate 1/error, distinct from error_trend/softmax already tested; moderate ranking stability favors stable aggregate weights over window-trend weights

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool4 weighted by w5' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.4641. Series context: trend strength 0.3088 and seasonal strength 0.0; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.47); 14 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 20.34.
